beats.say: An extortion email has arrived. Now let us practise the right steps in order.
The first two rules: do not pay and do not reply. A reply makes you a new target.
If you still use the password from the email, change it and turn on two-step verification.
If it came to work mail, report it to the security team. You are not to blame.

scenes.prompt: You received an extortion email. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Do not pay and do not reply
Report the email to the security team
Change the password from the email everywhere

scenes.explain: First stop, then report and change the password. Two-step verification protects the account even if an old password leaks.

scenes.title: Morning, work computer
scenes.intro: An extortion email notification pops up on your work computer. Choose the right move at every step.

title.text: Your password: Gunes2019. You have 48 hours

body.text: I have videos recorded with your camera. Send bitcoin or everyone will see them.

actions.label: Report
actions.feedback: Right. Reporting without paying or replying is the best first step.

actions.label: Reply: show me proof
actions.feedback: You replied, and the scammer at once sent a file called proof.

actions.label: Copy the bitcoin address and pay
actions.feedback: The money is gone and will not come back. People who pay usually get a new demand.

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: This is not proof, it is malware. Never open files from an extortion email.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. Do not open the file, and report the email to the security team.

actions.label: Scan with antivirus
actions.feedback: A good habit, but there is no need to keep this file. Delete it and report.

body.text: The password in the email was found in an old data leak.
New password: at least 15 characters, not used on other sites.

steps.say: This password is still used on some of your accounts.

actions.label: Change password
actions.feedback: Well done. The leaked password no longer opens this account, so change it on your other accounts too.

actions.label: Later
actions.feedback: Leaked passwords are tried again and again to open accounts. Do not put the change off.

body.text: Ask for the approval app on your phone at sign in, as well as the password?

actions.label: Turn on
actions.feedback: Right. Even if the password leaks, the second step protects the account.

actions.label: Not now
actions.feedback: Without two-step verification one password opens everything. Turn it on today.

body.text: No payment received. The videos go out tomorrow.

steps.say: A day later a new threat arrived.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. A repeated threat is a bluff too, so do not pay and do not reply.

actions.label: Report
actions.feedback: Well done. The security team can block the new emails as well.

actions.label: Reply: give me some time
actions.feedback: Negotiating gives the scammer hope. Do not reply, and report it.

nodes.text: Look, an extortion email came to my personal mail, and it shows my old password!
nodes.speaker: Narmin (your colleague) shows her phone
nodes.spoken: Look, <breath> an extortion email came to my personal mail, and it shows my old password!

choices.label: Stay calm, it is a mass bluff. Do not pay and do not reply
choices.feedback: Right. Calm, clear advice takes the panic down at once.

choices.label: Maybe pay half so they leave you alone
choices.feedback: People who pay get new demands. Money does not stop the threat.

choices.label: Reply and ask for proof
choices.feedback: A reply shows the address is active and brings more emails.

nodes.text: I still use that password on several sites, what should I do?
nodes.speaker: Narmin (your colleague)
nodes.spoken: I still use that password on several sites, uh, what should I do?

choices.label: Change it everywhere, use a different password for each site and turn on two-step verification
choices.feedback: Well done. Separate passwords stop one leak from spreading to every account.

choices.label: Change only this mailbox password, the rest does not matter
choices.feedback: The same password will be tried on other sites too. Change them all.

question.prompt: A teenage relative says someone is threatening to publish private videos of them and wants money. What should be done?

options.label: Never pay, go to the police
options.feedback: Right. Never pay, go to the police.

options.label: Pay once so it ends
options.feedback: Paying does not stop the threat. Never pay, go to the police.

options.label: Keep it secret and tell no one
options.feedback: Secrecy helps the person making threats. Never pay, go to the police.

scenes.explain: If a child or teenager is being threatened, never pay. Go to the police at once.

points: Do not pay, do not reply and do not open files from the email.
Change the leaked password everywhere and turn on two-step verification.
If a child is threatened, never pay and go to the police.
